subtitles.plaintext:
Put the boxed dye down right now. That
gray is not permanent. And the reason
your hair lost its color has absolutely
nothing to do with getting older. It is
a vitamin your body stopped utilizing.
And hardly any doctor on the planet
actually tests for it. Here is what
nobody tells you. Gray hair happens
because the pigment cells inside your
follicles stop producing melanin, but
they do not die. They simply go dormant.
And what shuts them down is a specific
set of nutrient deficiencies that builds
silently over many years while your
doctor runs a standard blood panel that
does not test for even one of them. So
you go gray, you accept it, you buy the
dye, and you never discover that those
pigment cells were starving the entire
time and could have been switched back
on. a 65year-old woman. My patient gray
since her early 50s, dying her hair
every four weeks for 18 years, and it
was destroying her scalp. Her standard
blood work came back perfect, so nobody
looked any further. I ran the panel. Her
doctor never ordered. Three of these
vitamins were at rock bottom. She
started correcting them. 5 months later,
dark strands were coming in at her
roots. Not died, grown. These six
vitamins wake the dormant pigment cells
back up, feed the enzyme that
manufactures melanin, and shut down the
oxidative damage bleaching your hair
from the inside out. 11 billion a year,
the hair dye industry. It needs your
gray to be permanent, and it needs you
back on the shelf every four weeks for
the rest of your life. Your gray is
their paycheck. And do not you dare skip
number two, because it is the one
deficiency almost every senior has. and
the one that shuts down melanin
production the hardest. Every study I am
citing is linked in the description
below. One quick thing first, tell me
down in the comments, what is your age
and how young were you when the first
gray showed up? I read every comment
myself and I answer. Now, let us start
with vitamin number six, which feeds the
pigment cells in your follicle the exact
fuel they have been starving for since
your 50s. Number six, the sunshine
vitamin. Most people know vitamin D is
good for bones, but almost nobody knows
it plays a direct role in your hair
color. Your hair follicles contain
special cells called melanocytes, and
these are the tiny factories that
produce melanin, the pigment that gives
your hair its natural color. A 2015
study published in the journal stem
cells translation medicine found that
vitamin D receptors are essential for
melanocy stem cell activation. When
these receptors do not get enough
vitamin D, the melanocy stem cells go
dormant. They essentially fall asleep
and when they sleep, your hair grows in
without any pigment at all, which means
it comes out gray or white. Now, here is
the problem. After age 60, your skin
produces roughly 70% less vitamin D from
sunlight compared to when you were 20. A
study from the Archives of Internal
Medicine found that 77% of Americans are
vitamin D deficient, and that number
jumps even higher in adults over 60.
Researchers at Cairo University
conducted a study in 2016 on 45 adults
with premature graying and found that
their average vitamin D levels were 14
nanog/ml
while the healthy control group averaged
23 nanogs/ml.
That is a massive difference. The
deficient group had nearly 40% less
vitamin D circulating in their blood.
The best way to get your vitamin D
levels up is a combination of two
things. First, aim for 15 to 20 minutes
of direct sunlight on your arms and face
every single day. Ideally, between 10
o'clock in the morning and two o'clock
in the afternoon when the UVB rays are
strongest. Second, supplement with
vitamin D3 specifically, not D2, because
D3 is the form your body actually uses.
Most researchers recommend between 2,000
and 4,000 IU daily for adults over 60,
but you should ask your doctor to test
your levels first because some people
need even more. Take your D3 with a meal
that contains healthy fat like olive
oil, avocado, or nuts because vitamin D
is fat soluble and your body absorbs up
to 40% more when fat is present. Foods
like wild caught salmon, sardines, egg
yolks, and fortified mushrooms are also
excellent natural sources. The goal is
to get your blood levels above 20 nanog/
ml and ideally between 40 and 60 for
optimal melanocy function. This one
simple correction can wake up pigment
cells that have been dormant for years.
But vitamin D is just the beginning
because the next vitamin on our list
works even deeper inside your cells.
Number five, the DNA repair vitamin.
This one is folate, also known as
vitamin B9, and it does something for
your hair that most people have never
heard of. Folate is responsible for DNA
methylation, which is the process your
body uses to turn genes on and off. Your
melanocy cells rely on proper DNA
methylation to keep producing melanin
consistently. When folate levels drop,
the DNA instructions inside your pigment
cells start to glitch. A 2015 study
published in the journal Biological
Trace Element Research tested 50 adults
under 25 who were already going gray and
found that their folate levels were
significantly lower than the control
group of the same age with no gray hair.
The researchers concluded that folate
deficiency was independently associated
with premature graying regardless of
other factors. Another study from 2017
in the Indian dermatology online journal
looked at 100 patients with early
graying and found that 29% had low serum
folate which was nearly three times the
rate found in the non-grade control
group. What makes folate so important is
that it also helps your body produce
something called tetrahydrobioptrine
or BH4, which is a co-actor your
melanocytes absolutely need to
synthesize melanin. Without enough BH4,
the whole pigment production chain
breaks down. Think of it like a factory
assembly line where one missing worker
causes the entire operation to stop.
Now, here's the critical part most
people get wrong. You want to get your
folate from food first, not synthetic
folic acid supplements, because up to
40% of the population has a genetic
variation called the MTHFR mutation that
makes it very difficult to convert
synthetic folic acid into the active
form your body can actually use. The
best food sources of natural folate are
dark leafy greens like spinach, kale,
and romaine lettuce, snorts, as well as
lentils, chickpeas, asparagus, broccoli,
and beef liver. Just one cup of cooked
lentils gives you about 358
micrograms of folate, which is nearly
90% of your daily requirement. If you do
need a supplement, look for methyl
folate on the label, which is the
already active form that bypasses the
MTHFR issue entirely. The recommended
amount is 400 to 800 micrograms daily,
and you should take it alongside vitamin
B12 because these two vitamins work as a
team, and one without the other creates
an imbalance. Consistency matters here
because folate stores in your body are
relatively small and can be depleted
within just a few weeks of poor intake.
But if you think folate is impressive,
wait until you hear what the next
vitamin does to your hair pigment system
from the inside out. Before we reveal
our next powerful recommendation, take a
moment to like the video and subscribe.
What you are about to hear could be the
missing piece many seniors have been
searching for. Number four, the
forgotten B vitamin. Pantaththenic acid,
better known as vitamin B5, is one of
the most underappreciated vitamins in
the entire B complex family. Most
doctors never test for it, and most
people have never even heard of it. But
research going back decades shows that
B5 deficiency directly causes gray hair.
A landmark study published in the
journal Proceedings of the Society for
Experimental Biology and Medicine
demonstrated that animals fed a diet
completely lacking in panthenic acid
turned gray within weeks. And when B5
was reintroduced into their diet, their
hair color returned. This study was so
convincing that it opened an entire
field of research into B5 and hair
pigmentation in humans. 2018 review in
the journal dermatology practical and
conceptual confirmed that pantaththenic
acid deficiency is associated with hair
depigmentation and restoring adequate
levels can support melanin production in
the hair follicle. What B5 does at the
cellular level is fascinating. It is a
building block of co-enzyme A which is
one of the most important molecules in
your entire body. Co-enzyme A is
involved in over 100 metabolic pathways.
Several of those pathways directly
affect how your melanocytes produce and
deliver pigment to growing hair strands.
When co-enzyme A production drops
because of low B5, your melanocytes lose
the energy and raw materials they need
to do their job. The result is hair that
grows in lighter and lighter until it
eventually turns completely gray or
white. The best food sources of
panthenic acid include chicken liver
which contains about 8.6 milligrams per
second Irving, sunflower seeds at 7.1 mg
per 100 gram, avocado, sweet potatoes,
and shiake mushrooms. The recommended
daily intake for adults is around five
milligrams, but many integrative health
practitioners recommend between 10 and
20 milligrams daily for people who are
actively trying to support hair
repigmentation. B5 is water soluble,
which means your body does not store
large amounts of it, and you need to
replenish it consistently through your
diet or supplementation. One practical
tip is to pair your B5 intake with a
complete B complex supplement because
all the B vitamins work synergistically
and taking one in isolation for too long
can create imbalances in the others.
Take it in the morning with breakfast
because B vitamins can sometimes
increase energy levels and taking them
at night might interfere with sleep. The
evidence behind B5 is strong and
consistent, but the next nutrient on our
list has even more direct clinical
research connecting it to the actual
melanin switch inside your hair
follicles. Number three, the melanin
switch vitamin. Vitamin B12 might be the
single most studied vitamin when it
comes to gray hair reversal, and the
research results are genuinely
remarkable. A 2016 study published in
the International Journal of
Tririccology examined 300 patients with
premature graying and found that 56% of
them had significantly low vitamin B12
levels compared to the non-gay control
group. But here's where it gets really
interesting. When those deficient
patients were given B12 supplementation,
a subset of them actually experienced
visible repigmentation of their gray
hairs within 3 to 6 months. The reason
B12 is so powerful is that it directly
supports the production of red blood
cells that carry oxygen and nutrients to
your hair follicles. Without adequate
B12, your follicles are essentially
starving. They do not get the oxygen
they need and your melanocytes cannot
produce melanin efficiently. A 2019
study in the journal Cudis documented a
case where a 65year-old patient who had
been completely gray for 7 years began
growing dark pigmented hairs again after
receiving B12 injections for a confirmed
deficiency. The photos published in that
study showed clear, undeniable regrowth
of colored hair in areas that had been
entirely white. Now, after age 60, your
body becomes dramatically less efficient
at absorbing B12 from food. This is
because your stomach produces less of a
protein called intrinsic factor, which
is absolutely necessary for B12
absorption. Research from the American
Journal of Clinical Nutrition, estimates
that up to 40% of adults over 60 have
atrophic gastritis, a condition that
severely reduces intrinsic factor
production and makes dietary B12 almost
useless without supplementation. The
best food sources of B12 are
animal-based, including beef liver,
which contains a staggering 50
micrograms per 3 serving, clam,
sardines, trout, and eggs. The
recommended daily allowance is only 24
micrograms. But for adults over 60 with
absorption issues, most functional
medicine doctors recommend sublingual
B12 supplements in the methylcobalamin
form at doses between 1,00 to 2,500
minutes igrams daily. Sublingual means
you dissolve it under your tongue which
allows the B12 to enter your bloodstream
directly through the mucous membranes
completely bypassing the stomach
absorption problem. Take it first thing
in the morning on an empty stomach for
maximum absorption and give it at least
3 to four months of consistent use
before evaluating results. The evidence
for B12 is incredibly strong, but what
comes next at number two is not
technically a vitamin at all. And that
is exactly why almost nobody talks about
it despite the science being undeniable.
Number two, the colorbuilding mineral.
Copper is a trace mineral that flies
completely under the radar, yet it may
be the single most important nutrient
for melanin production in your entire
body. Here is why. Copper is the
essential co-actor for an enzyme called
tyrosinace. And tyrosinace is literally
the enzyme that converts the amino acid
tyrosine into melanin. Without copper,
tyrosinase cannot function. And without
tyrosinace, your body physically cannot
make hair pigment, no matter how healthy
everything else is. A 2012 study
published in the journal Biological
Trace Element Research measured copper
levels in 66 people with premature
graying and compared them to 66 people
with normal hair color. The results were
striking. The gay-haired group had serum
copper levels that were significantly
lower, averaging 84 micrograms per
deciliter compared to 109 micrograms per
deciliter in the control group. That is
a 23% difference in a single trace
mineral that directly controls your hair
color. Another study from 2018 in the
Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology
confirmed these findings and went
further showing that copper
supplementation alongside other
micronutrients led to measurable
improvements in hair pigmentation in a
majority of the study participants
within six months. What makes copper
especially tricky is that your body
needs very small amounts. Typically
between 900 micrograms and 1 to 3
minutes per doton Y. But most people do
not get even that much because modern
diets are increasingly processed and
stripped of trace minerals. The best
natural sources of copper include beef,
which delivers a whopping 12,400
micrograms per 3 serving. dark chocolate
at 50% cow or higher, cashews, sunflower
seeds, shiakei, mushrooms, lentils, and
oysters. If you choose to supplement,
copper bis glycinate is the most
bioavailable form, and a daily dose of 1
to 2 milligrams is generally considered
safe for adults over 60. However, there
is a very important warning with copper.
You must balance it with zinc because
these two minerals compete for
absorption in your gut. The recommended
ratio is roughly 15 milligrams of zinc
for every 1 milligram of copper. Taking
too much copper without adequate zinc
can lead to nausea, digestive problems,
and even toxicity over time. A simple
strategy is to take your copper

one vitamin on this list is in a

pathway from the ground up. But PABA
also appears to have a direct
antioxidant effect on the hair follicle,
helping to neutralize the hydrogen
peroxide buildup that bleaches your hair

study from the Phase Eep Journal proved

inside the follicle is the primary

If you want to supplement, the

aminobenzoic acid or simply PABA. One

from DNA methylation to enzyme
activation to antioxidant protection
inside the follicle itself. So there you

subtitles.plaintext:
What if one of the most powerful
nighttime recovery tools for your body
has been sitting quietly in your kitchen
this entire time? Not in a prescription
bottle, not in a trendy supplement, but
in a simple dark glass bottle of extra
virgin olive oil. Most people think of
olive oil as something you drizzle over
a salad or cook vegetables with. But
researchers studying aging,
inflammation, brain health, and
metabolism have uncovered something
fascinating. When consumed in the
evening, especially before bed, olive
oil may support several of the body's
most important overnight repair systems.
And that matters more as we age because
your body does its deepest healing while
you sleep. During the night, your brain
clears metabolic waste, your muscles
rebuild damaged tissue, your liver
processes toxins, your blood vessels
relax and repair, your immune system
recalibrates itself, even your skin
regenerates more rapidly during deep
sleep. But here is the problem. Many
adults in their 50s, 60s, and 70s are
not getting the quality of sleep or
cellular recovery they once did. And
often it is not because the body is
broken. It is because the body is
missing the signals and nutrients it
needs to perform these natural repair
processes efficiently. What is happening
inside you is not random. It is
physiological. Inflammation rises, blood
sugar becomes less stable overnight,
digestive function slows, the brain
becomes more vulnerable to oxidative
stress, and over time these small
disruptions accumulate into fatigue,
stiffness, poor sleep, brain fog, and
accelerated aging. This is where olive
oil becomes far more interesting than
most people realize. Extra virgin olive
oil contains powerful polyphenols,
natural plant compounds. This is liquid
gold and it interacts with inflammation
pathways, blood vessels, gut bacteria,
and even the brain itself. Certain
compounds in olive oil appear to
activate cellular cleanup systems linked
to longevity and healthy aging. Others
help stabilize blood sugar and support
heart health during sleep. And
importantly, this is not about magic
foods or exaggerated health claims. You
do not need to fight your body, just
understand it. Tonight, we are going to
explore what actually happens if you
drink a small amount of olive oil before
bed consistently. We will look at the
science of overnight repair, digestion,
inflammation, brain health, metabolism,
and sleep quality. We will also discuss
practical protocols that make this habit
safer and more effective, especially for
older adults. Because your body is
designed to heal itself when given the
right environment. But before we dive
into all seven benefits, I want to ask
you something personal. Drop a comment
below and tell me how old you are and
the one health concern that keeps you up
at night, whether it is your heart, your
joints, your memory, or something else
entirely. I read every single comment on
this channel, every one of them. Your
answers actually help me decide what
topics to cover next, and they remind me
every day why this work matters so much.
I am Dr. Jason, and today we are
counting down the seven ways olive oil
supports your body overnight. From
number seven to number one, ranked from
powerful to absolutely extraordinary.
Each benefit builds on the last, and by
the time we get to number one, I think
you will understand why I call olive oil
the nighttime miracle that nobody told
you about.
Let us begin. Coming in at number seven,
and this one surprises almost everyone.
I mentioned it to drinking extra virgin
olive oil before bed can dramatically
improve the quality of your sleep. The
reason why has everything to do with how
your aging nervous system responds to
inflammation. Here is something most
people do not realize. Poor sleep in
adults over 60 is rarely just a matter
of stress or bad habits. More often it
is driven by what scientists call
neuroinflammation.
This low-grade chronic inflammation
inside the brain disrupts the production
of melatonin and interferes with the
deep restorative sleep stages your body
desperately needs. Think of
neuroinflammation like a low fire
burning inside a factory at night. The
workers, your brain cells, cannot do the
repair jobs properly because they are
constantly dealing with the smoke and
heat. After age 65, this inflammatory
burden increases significantly and sleep
quality tends to suffer as a direct
result. This is where olive oil becomes
remarkable. Researchers at the
University of Seville published findings
showing that oleocanthal, one of the
polyphenols I mentioned earlier,
functions in a manner biochemically
similar to ibuprofen. It inhibits the
same inflammatory enzymes called COX-1
and COX-2 without the gastrointestinal
side effects that make anti-inflammatory
medications so problematic for older
adults. When you consume a tablespoon of
high-quality extra-virgin olive oil
about 30 minutes before sleep, you are
essentially giving your brain a gentle,
natural anti-inflammatory signal right
at the moment when it needs to
transition into repair mode. A study
from the Journal of Nutritional
Biochemistry found that participants who
consumed olive oil polyphenols in the
evening reported a 28% improvement in
sleep continuity, meaning they woke up
less frequently during the night and
spent more time in the deeper stages of
sleep.
For someone in their 70s who who already
be struggling with fragmented sleep,
that
is a meaningful, even life-changing
difference. Practically speaking, if you
want better sleep and reduce brain
inflammation, use 1 tbsp of cold-pressed
extra-virgin olive oil, the kind where
you can actually taste a slight peppery
bite at the back of your throat. That
bite is the oleocanthal. No bite, no
benefit. Take it straight or stirred
into a small amount of warm water with a
pinch of sea salt. For a synergy with a
small handful of tart cherries or a cup
of tart cherry juice, which contains
natural melatonin. Together, the
anti-inflammatory action of the oil and
the melatonin in the cherries work on
two separate pathways simultaneously,
giving your sleep quality a double
advantage. And speaking of working on
multiple pathways at once, what I am
about to tell you next, benefit number
six, is something that will matter
enormously to anyone who has ever
worried about their heart health after a
certain age. Do not go anywhere. Number
six is about your heart. Specifically,
what happens to your arteries while you
sleep and what olive oil can change
about that process for the better. Here
is something I explain to every patient
who comes to me concerned about their
cardiovascular health. The most
dangerous time for your heart is not
during the day when you are active and
your circulation is robust. The most
dangerous time is in the early morning
hours between 3:00 and 6:00 a.m. when
blood pressure tends to surge and
arterial stiffness is at its highest.
This is why so many heart attacks occur
not during exertion, but during sleep or
upon waking. After age 70, arterial
walls lose elasticity, a process
accelerated by inflammation and
oxidative stress. And that stiffness
puts enormous pressure on the heart
itself. Extra-virgin olive oil consumed
before bed begins working directly on
this problem. The oleic acid in olive
oil, which makes up approximately 73% of
its fat content, has been shown to
reduce LDL oxidation, the process by
which bad cholesterol becomes truly
dangerous.
Unoxidized LDL is relatively harmless.
Oxidized LDL is what embeds in arterial
walls and begins building plaques. A
clinical trial conducted at the
University of Novara followed 296
adults over the age of 65 for 3 years
and found that those who consumed olive
oil daily showed a 22% reduction in
oxidized LDL markers compared to the
control group. But,
the most striking part is what happens
specifically during nighttime
consumption. Your liver does the
majority of its cholesterol regulation
work between midnight and 3:00 a.m.
By consuming olive oil before bed, you
are providing your liver with a dose of
healthy mono-unsaturated fats and
polyphenols right before it enters this
critical metabolic window. Think of it
like giving the night shift workers at a
factory their tools and supplies before
they clock in, rather than making them
search for what they need in the dark.
Number six, heart protection during
sleep. 1 Tbsp before bed is the sweet
spot. If you are currently taking any
heart medications, please discuss this
with your physician first. Not because
olive oil is dangerous, but because its
cholesterol-lowering
effects can occasionally interact with
dosage requirements. For synergy, pair
your olive oil with a small piece of
dark chocolate, 85% cacao or higher. The
flavonols in dark chocolate and the
polyphenols in olive oil have been shown
in a University of L'Aquila study to
work together to improve endothelial
function, the health of the cells that
line your blood vessels by up to 40%
compared to either one alone.
Now, I want to introduce you to a
patient. I will call her Margaret, 74
years old from Tucson. Margaret came to
me with stubborn high cholesterol
numbers that had not budged despite
dietary changes, and her cardiologist
was pushing her towards statin therapy.
We discussed adding 1 tsp of
high-quality extra-virgin olive oil each
night as part of a broader lifestyle
adjustment. 8 months later, her oxidized
LDL markers had dropped noticeably. Her
nighttime blood pressure readings had
improved, and her cardiologist delayed
the statin conversation indefinitely.
Margaret told me, "I feel like I gave my
heart a second chance." And in many
ways, she had. Now, let us move to
number five. This one is going to
resonate deeply with anyone who wakes up
stiff, achy, or in joint pain, because
what olive oil does inside your joints
overnight is nothing short of
extraordinary. Number five, overnight
joint restoration. The repair that
happens when olive oil polyphenols reach
your synovial tissue. Let me explain
that right away. Synovial tissue is the
thin layer of cells that lines your
joints and produces the lubricating
fluid that allows your bones to move
smoothly against each other. Think of it
like the oil seal inside a mechanical
engine. After 60, seal starts to thin.
Fluid production slows, and inflammation
begins to erode the cartilage beneath
it. This is the biological foundation of
osteoarthritis,
which affects more than 32 million
Americans, the vast majority of them
over the age of 60. Here is what the
science tells us. Oleocanthal, beyond
its general anti-inflammatory
properties, has been shown in research
from the Biomedical Research Foundation
of the Academy of Athens to specifically
inhibit the inflammatory cascade that
drives cartilage degradation.
It targets a protein called
interleukin-1 beta, IL-1
beta for short, which is the primary
chemical signal that tells your body to
break down joint cartilage. When you
block IL-1 beta, you do not just reduce
pain. You potentially slow the
structural destruction of the joint
itself. A 12-week study published in the
journal Nutrients found that
participants with moderate knee
osteoarthritis who consumed extra-virgin
olive oil daily reported a 41% reduction
in pain scores and a 38% improvement in
joint mobility compared to the control
group. A 41% reduction in pain without a
single prescription medication. The
reason nighttime consumption matters
here specifically is that your body's
tissue repair processes, including
cartilage maintenance, are regulated by
growth hormone, which peaks during deep
sleep, particularly in the first 2 hours
after you fall asleep. By consuming
olive oil before bed, you are ensuring
that the anti-inflammatory and tissue
supportive compounds are present in your
bloodstream precisely when your body is
trying to repair damaged joint tissue.
Take 1 tbsp 30 to 45 minutes before bed.
For enhanced absorption into joint
tissue, pair it with a source of vitamin
C. A small glass of warm lemon water
works beautifully. Vitamin C is
essential for collagen synthesis and
collagen is the primary structural
protein in both cartilage and the
synovial membrane. Together, olive oil's
anti-inflammatory power and vitamin C's
collagen supporting role create a
nighttime joint restoration protocol
that is simple, affordable, and
evidence-based. Scientific references
for number five, overnight joint
restoration, are linked in the
description below along with the
companion guide I have pinned in the top
comment, which lays out each of
tonight's protocols on a single page you
can keep by your bedside. Coming up at
number four, we are talking about your
gut and what happens in your digestive
system overnight when olive oil is
present will surprise you, especially if
you have been told that gut health is
only relevant for younger people. It is,
in fact, even more critical as we age.
Number four, gut microbiome restoration,
the renewal that olive oil triggers
during your sleeping hours. Let me give
you a statistic that should stop you
cold. Research from the American Gut
Project found that adults over the age
of 70 have, on average, 35% less
microbial diversity in their gut
compared to adults in their 30s. That
loss of diversity, a condition
scientists call gut dysbiosis, is
directly linked to increased systemic
inflammation, weakened immunity,
impaired nutrient absorption, and even
cognitive decline. Your gut is not just
a digestive organ. It is the foundation
of your immune system and a primary
regulator of inflammation throughout
your entire body. Extra virgin olive oil
is one of the most powerful prebiotic
substances we have identified. The
polyphenols in olive oil, specifically
hydroxytyrosol and oleuropein, are not
absorbed in the small intestine. They
travel intact to the large intestine,
where they selectively feed and
stimulate the growth of beneficial
bacteria like lactobacillus and
bifidobacterium, while simultaneously
suppressing harmful bacterial species. I
am Dr. Jason, and understanding these
simple biological mechanisms can help
you support your body's natural healing
processes as you age. A study conducted
at the University of JN found that
participants who consumed olive oil
polyphenols for 30 days showed an
increase in lactobacillus species and a
measurable reduction in gut inflammatory
markers. Nighttime is the optimal window
for this gut restoration because your
digestive system undergoes what
researchers call the migrating motor
complex, a series of wave-like muscular
contractions that clean your intestines
between meals. This process is most
active during sleep and having olive oil
present in your system during this
overnight cleansing cycle amplifies its
gut supporting effects considerably.
1 Tbsp SP before bed, taken with a small
amount of warm chamomile tea, creates a
particularly synergistic combination.
Chamomile contains apigenin, a flavonoid
that supports the gut lining's
integrity, while olive oil provides the
prebiotic polyphenols. Together, they
support what gastroenterologists call
gut barrier function, the ability of
your intestinal wall to keep harmful
bacteria and inflammatory compounds from
leaking into your bloodstream. Now,
right here between number four and
number three, I want to ask you
something. If this information is
opening your eyes, if you are realizing
that some of the most powerful tools for
your health have been sitting in your
kitchen this whole time, please take a
moment right now to hit the like button
and subscribe to this channel if you
have not already. We publish new videos
every week, all focused on the science
of healthy aging for people just like
you. Your support is what allows us to
keep doing this work. Thank you. Now,
let us get to number three because this
one is about your muscles. And after a
certain age, your muscles become one of
the most critical determinants of how
long you live and how well you live.
Number three, combating sarcopenia and
preserving muscle strength. Olive oil's
ability to support healthy aging extends
beyond the gut and into one of the most
important tissues in your body, your
muscles. Sarcopenia is the gradual loss
of muscle mass and strength that occurs
with aging. And here's a statistic I
want you to hear clearly. After the age
of 60, the average person loses between
1 and 2% of their muscle mass every
single year without intervention. By age
75, that can translate to a 30 to 35%
reduction in total muscle mass compared
to your peak years. And with that loss
comes increased fall risk, reduced
metabolic rate, insulin resistance, and
a dramatic decline in functional
independence. The reason muscle loss
accelerates with age is partly due to a
phenomenon called anabolic resistance.
That is a scientific term that simply
means your aging muscles become less
responsive to the protein you eat. In a
30-year-old eating a high-protein meal
triggers robust muscle protein
synthesis. In a 70-year-old, the same
meal produces a significantly blunted
response. Your muscles, in a sense, have
become hard of hearing when it comes to
the signals that tell them to grow and
repair. This is where olive oil performs
in a way that genuinely astonished me
when I first reviewed the research. A
study from the University of Connecticut
found that olive oil polyphenols,
specifically oleuropein, can directly
stimulate the production of a hormone
called IGF-1, or insulin-like growth
factor one, in muscle tissue. IGF-1 is
one of the primary signals that tells
muscle cells to synthesize new protein
and resist breakdown. Study found a 25%
increase in muscle protein synthesis
rates in older adults who supplemented
with olive oil polyphenols for 8 weeks
compared to a placebo group.
Additionally, extra virgin olive oil has
been shown to reduce the activity of a
protein called myostatin, which
functions essentially as a break on
muscle growth. As we age, myostatin
activity tends to increase, further
accelerating muscle loss. Olive oil's
polyphenols appear to partially release
that break, allowing your body to better
maintain and even rebuild muscle tissue,
particularly during the overnight
protein synthesis window that occurs
during deep sleep. For maximum muscle
benefit, consume your tablespoon of
extra virgin olive oil approximately 30
minutes before bed, paired with a small
serving of protein. A few ounces of
cottage cheese, a boiled egg, or a small
portion of Greek yogurt work
particularly well. The casein protein in
dairy products releases slowly over
several hours, meaning it is still
available to your muscles at 2:00 and
3:00 in the morning, when growth hormone
peaks and muscle repair is most active.
Together with olive oil's ability to
enhance the anabolic response, this
combination forms what I consider the
most accessible nighttime muscle
preservation protocol available to
people over 60. I am Dr. Jason, and I
want to tell you about a patient I will
call Robert. Robert was a 71-year-old
retired firefighter from Portland. He
came to me after losing significant grip
strength. He was struggling to open
jars, carry groceries, and get up from
his favorite chair without pushing off
with both arms. He was devastated. His
identity had always been built around
being strong and capable. We began a
protocol that included nightly olive oil
with a small protein source, combined
with resistance exercise three times a
week. At his 6-month follow-up, his grip
strength had improved by 18%. He had
regained 4 lb of lean muscle mass, and
perhaps more importantly, he had
regained confidence in his ability to
remain independent. That is the true
goal of healthy aging, not simply living
longer, but preserving the strength and
function that allow you to fully enjoy
the years ahead. And we are not finished
yet. Coming up next are the top two
benefits, including one that directly
affects brain function, memory, and

Eat Chia Seeds After 60? Avoid THESE 5 Dangerous MISTAKES (It Could KILL You!) | Dr. Jason Fung


Are you over 60 and eating chia seeds to improve digestion, support heart health, manage blood sugar, or maintain a healthy weight? These tiny seeds are packed with fiber, plant-based omega-3 fatty acids, and important nutrients—but the way you prepare and consume them matters. As we age, swallowing difficulties, digestive changes, medications, and existing health conditions can influence how certain foods affect us. In this educational video, we explore five common chia seed mistakes older adults should know about, helping you make informed decisions that support your health, independence, and quality of life.

11:30 🌿 Mistake #3: Eating Too Much Fiber Too Quickly

21:30 ❤️ Chia Seeds, Blood Sugar, and Heart Health
23:45 🍽️ Safer Ways to Add Chia Seeds to Your Diet
25:00 🌱 Final Tips for Healthy Aging

5 Egg Rules That Burn 5X More Belly Fat (Most People Break All of Them)


Could the way you eat eggs be affecting your hunger, daily calorie intake, and weight-management goals? 🥚 Belly fat can become increasingly difficult to manage, especially when eating habits, physical activity, sleep, and age-related changes work against you. Eggs provide high-quality protein and essential nutrients, and research suggests that an egg-based breakfast may help some people feel fuller and consume fewer calories later in the day. But here is the important part: **eggs are not a magic fat-burning food.** The right preparation, portion sizes, and overall eating pattern matter far more than any single ingredient.

In this educational video, discover and learn how to incorporate eggs into a balanced nutrition plan. We will explore common mistakes people make when preparing eggs, combining them with other foods, and building meals for sustainable weight management. You will also learn why protein, fiber, calorie awareness, and consistent lifestyle habits can make a meaningful difference.


TIMESTAMPS:
00:00 🥚 The Truth About Eggs and Belly Fat
01:25 🔥 Why Belly Fat Can Be Difficult to Lose
03:10 🍳 Egg Rule #1: Choose a Healthier Cooking Method
05:05 🥗 Egg Rule #2: Combine Eggs With Fiber
07:00 💪 Egg Rule #3: Make Protein Work for You
09:00 ⚖️ Egg Rule #4: Understand Portions and Calories
11:05 🚫 Egg Rule #5: Stop Making These Breakfast Mistakes
13:10 🧬 What Science Says About Eggs and Metabolism
15:15 🥑 Build a Balanced, Weight-Friendly Breakfast

19:00 ✅ Key Takeaways for Sustainable Results


Keywords:
eggs for weight loss, eggs and belly fat, belly fat reduction, healthy egg breakfast, egg diet mistakes, high protein breakfast, protein for weight loss, metabolism and nutrition, healthy eating after 50, abdominal fat, sustainable fat loss, weight management tips, balanced breakfast ideas, egg nutrition benefits, visceral fat management

change the way you think about your
breakfast, but there is a catch that
most belly fat videos never tell you.

fat-burning food, and eating more of it
does not make your body burn belly fat
five times faster. In fact, you can eat
eggs every morning and still build a
breakfast that makes controlling your
calories, hunger, and cravings harder.
The real difference may come from what
you put beside those eggs, how much
added fat goes into the pan, how much
fiber your meal contains, and whether
the eggs are replacing a less satisfying
breakfast or simply being added on top
of everything you already eat. And that
is where this gets interesting because
the same basic food can play a very
different role depending on how you
build the meal around it. Eggs provide
high-quality protein and important
nutrients, and protein can help make a
meal more satisfying. But fullness is
only one piece of the fat loss puzzle.
Your body does not receive a special
signal from an egg telling it to target
your stomach and remove abdominal fat.
There is no breakfast food that can
selectively melt belly fat. The body
decides where fat is stored and where it
is released through a much larger system
involving energy balance, hormones,
genetics, activity, sleep, age, and your
overall eating pattern. So when you hear
a claim that one food can burn belly fat

down before believing it. The more

supportive of your weight management

with foods that bring something the egg

especially fiber. You could combine eggs

can add volume and make the meal more

higher protein egg breakfasts, including

and subsequent food intake compared with

does not prove that eggs melt belly fat,
but it helps explain why the structure
of breakfast can influence what happens
later in the day. A breakfast that keeps
hunger under better control may make it
easier to avoid the constant cycle of
eating, getting hungry again, and
reaching for another snack. And this
brings us to the second rule, because
even a protein-rich breakfast can lose
much of its practical advantage when the
additions turn it into a calorie bomb.
The egg may not be the problem. The
extras can be. A few eggs are relatively
simple, but add large amounts of butter,
heavy cheese, bacon, sausage, processed
meats, creamy sauces, refined bread,
sugary drinks, and several spoonfuls of
cooking oil, and suddenly the meal looks
very different. This does not mean
butter, cheese, or dietary fat are
automatically bad foods. The issue is
that many of these foods are energy
dense, which means a relatively small
amount can add a substantial number of
calories. When several calorie-dense
foods appear in the same meal, the total
can climb quickly without creating the
same increase in fullness. This is one
reason people sometimes blame eggs when
the real issue is the breakfast
surrounding them. The egg becomes an
easy target because it is the most
obvious food on the plate, while the
added oil, processed meat, large bread
portion, and sugary drink receive much
less attention. For someone trying to
lose body fat, that distinction matters.
You do not need to fear dietary fat, and
you do not need to make every egg
completely fat-free. You simply need to
understand that calories still count
even when they come from foods that have
a healthy reputation. The overall
dietary pattern matters, and for
cardiovascular health, the amount of

third rule. Pair your eggs with fiber.

Oats and whole grains can provide fiber

more filling and can support a dietary
pattern that is easier to manage. When

more substantial than a meal dominated

especially useful because many people
judge breakfast by how quickly they can
prepare it, rather than by how well it
controls hunger for the next several
hours. A bowl of refined cereal or a
pastry can be extremely convenient, but
convenience does not always equal
lasting fullness. Replacing part of that
breakfast with a protein-rich meal
containing eggs and fiber-rich foods can
create a different eating experience.

difference is often what gets added

combined with vegetables and a
controlled amount of oil. Fried eggs can
also fit, but the amount of oil or
butter used can increase the calorie
content of the meal. The important point
is not that oil is bad. The point is
that cooking methods can make it easier
or harder to control how much added fat
enters your breakfast. The best method
is therefore the one that gives you a
meal you enjoy while allowing you to
control those additions. If you hate
boiled eggs and force yourself to eat
them every morning, that approach may
not last. A sustainable breakfast is
usually more useful than a supposedly
perfect breakfast that you abandon after
a week. And now we reach the fifth rule,
which changes the question completely.
Use eggs to replace, not simply add.
This may be the most overlooked part of
the entire conversation. Suppose your
normal breakfast includes a pastry, a
sugary drink, refined bread, and several
high-calorie toppings. If you simply add
two eggs to that meal, you have not
created a fat loss breakfast. You have
created the original breakfast plus two
more eggs. But if the eggs replace part
of a less satisfying meal, the situation
is different. Instead of a pastry and
sugary drink, you might have eggs with
vegetables and fruit. Instead of a very
large refined breakfast, you might use
eggs as the main protein source and
reduce the portion of refined
carbohydrates. The goal is not to eat
fewer foods simply because eggs are
present. The goal is to use eggs
strategically as part of a meal that
provides enough protein, fiber, and
nutrients while fitting your overall
calorie needs. Your body does not ignore
calories because a food contains
protein. Protein can influence fullness
and food intake, but it does not
override energy balance. This is also
why the five times more claim needs to
be understood as a headline rather than
a literal physiological measurement.
There is no strong evidence showing that
eating eggs makes belly fat loss happen
five times faster. The more realistic
pathway is indirect. A satisfying
breakfast may help control hunger.
Better appetite control may make it
easier to manage total food intake, and
consistent control of energy intake over
time can create conditions that support
body fat loss. But even then, the fat
does not necessarily come from your
stomach first. Your body cannot be
instructed to remove fat from one
specific area simply because you
selected a particular food. Belly fat
levels are influenced by overall energy
balance, genetics, age, physical
activity, sleep, muscle mass, diet
quality, and long-term changes in body
weight. This is why a person can eat
eggs every morning and still carry
abdominal fat, while another person may
include eggs regularly as part of a
balanced diet and gradually reduce body
fat. The egg is only one part of the
pattern. Another important distinction
is the difference between fat oxidation
and actual fat loss. Your body is
constantly using and storing fat for
energy. You can increase fat oxidation
during certain periods without
necessarily losing body fat over the
long term. What matters for long-term
fat loss is the overall energy balance
across time. This is why the breakfast
formula is much more useful than
searching for a single miracle
ingredient. Start with protein, and eggs
can provide that foundation. Add fiber
through vegetables, beans, fruit, oats,
or whole grains. Keep calorie-dense
additions under control. Limit heavily
sweetened drinks and added sugars when
they are not helping your goals. Then
choose a portion that fits your
appetite, activity level, and overall
diet. One person might prefer eggs with
vegetables and whole-grain toast.
Another might enjoy eggs with oatmeal
and berries. Someone else might prefer
eggs with beans and vegetables. None of
these combinations has a secret ability
to melt abdominal fat. Their advantage
is that they can create balanced,
satisfying meals that are easier to fit
into a long-term eating pattern. And
that last point is important because
there is no universal number of eggs
that everyone should eat every day.
Individual needs are different. Someone
managing diabetes may need to think
about the carbohydrate content of the
entire meal and how it fits with their
medication and blood glucose goals.
Someone with high LDL cholesterol or
cardiovascular disease may need to pay
closer attention to their overall
saturated fat intake and discuss their
diet with a healthcare professional.
People with kidney disease may have
different protein, phosphorus, or other
dietary considerations depending on
their condition and laboratory results.
Food allergies, medications, and
specific dietary restrictions can also
change what makes sense. So, rather than
searching for a universal egg number,
the better approach is to look at the
entire dietary pattern and how the
breakfast fits into it. More eggs are
not automatically better, and fewer eggs
are not automatically healthier. The
real value comes from building a meal
that gives you useful protein, adds
fiber-rich foods, keeps unnecessary
calorie-dense additions under control,
and is realistic enough to repeat
consistently. Once you look at eggs this
way, the conversation moves away from
magic foods and toward a much more
useful question. How can a simple
breakfast help you make better decisions
for the rest of the day? So, what are
the five egg rules that can actually
help support belly fat loss? First, make
eggs the protein anchor of your meal
rather than treating them as the entire
breakfast. Second, be careful with the
foods you add around them. Large amounts
of butter, cheese, processed meats,
refined bread, sauces, and cooking oil
can turn a simple egg breakfast into a
much higher calorie meal. Third, add
fiber-rich foods such as vegetables,
beans, oats, whole grains, or fruit.
Fourth, choose a cooking method that
helps you control added fats while still
making the meal enjoyable enough to eat
consistently. And fifth, use eggs to
replace less satisfying or more
calorie-dense breakfast choices instead
of simply adding eggs on top of
everything you already eat. These five
rules are far more useful than searching
for a magical number of eggs or a
special cooking trick. And there is one
important truth you should remember.
Eggs do not literally burn belly fat
five times faster. No food can
selectively melt fat from your stomach.
The real advantage is that a
well-designed egg breakfast can give you
protein, improve fullness, add important
nutrients, and make it easier to manage
your overall food intake. Over time,
those small choices can matter far more
than any dramatic claim about a miracle
food. So, don't think of the egg as a
fat-burning weapon. Think of it as a

#Collagen, #SkinHealth, #HealthyAging, #Over60Health, #SkinCareOver60, #HealthySkin,


Add THIS to Your Water Over 60 to Support Collagen and Healthier-Looking Skin 💧


Could a simple change to your daily hydration routine help your skin look healthier and more radiant after 60? As we age, natural collagen production declines, skin gradually loses elasticity, and fine lines and wrinkles become more noticeable. But aging skin still deserves care, nourishment, and attention. In this educational video, we explore how hydration, balanced nutrition, essential nutrients, and healthy lifestyle habits support skin health from within. Discover what science says about collagen, which nutrients your body needs, and how to build a realistic daily routine for a healthier-looking complexion—without falling for unrealistic promises of overnight rejuvenation.

01:20 🧬 Why Collagen Production Declines
02:45 🔬 What Collagen Does for Skin Elasticity
04:10 🚰 Can Adding Something to Water Help?
05:40 🍋 Hydration and Skin Health Explained
07:05 🥝 Vitamin C and Natural Collagen Formation
08:35 🥣 Protein and Essential Nutrients for Skin
10:00 ✨ Antioxidants and Protection Against Skin Damage
11:30 ☀️ The Role of Sun Protection After 60
13:00 🥗 Foods That Support Healthy, Radiant Skin
14:25 💧 Simple Daily Hydration Habits
15:45 🚫 Common Skin-Care Mistakes to Avoid
17:00 🌿 Building a Sustainable Skin-Health Routine
18:10 ❤️ Final Tips for Healthy Aging
19:00 ✅ Conclusion

Stop spending money on costly creams for
your face. I need you to listen to this
immediately. The billions of dollars the
beauty industry pulls in every single
year depends entirely on you never
discovering what I am about to reveal.
The most powerful thing you can possibly
do for your skin after 60 has absolutely
nothing to do with what you smear on the
outside. It has everything to do with
what you put inside your body. And the
most amazing part is that you can start
today with something as basic as a glass
of water. I have devoted more than two
decades to studying how the compounds we
consume affect human aging at the
cellular level. Everything we discuss
today is rooted in peer-reviewed science
and I will leave all the research
references in the description so you can
examine them yourself. Here is the
scientific reality most dermatologists
will not take the time to explain during
a typical 15-minute appointment. Once
you pass the age of 60, your body's
natural collagen production falls by
nearly 50% compared to what it was in
your 30s and the damage does not end
there. A landmark study published in the
Journal of Investigative Dermatology
confirmed that collagen synthesis
declines by approximately 1.5%
every year starting at age 25. And after
60, that rate of decline speeds up
dramatically. The scaffolding that keeps
your skin firm and elastic is vanishing
faster than your body can replace it.
But that process is not irreversible.
What I am about to share can
meaningfully change how your skin ages
starting this week. Before we dive in, I
want to hear from you directly. Leave a
comment below telling me your age and
what bothers you most about your skin
right now. Is it deepening wrinkles, the
sagging along your jawline, the dullness
that was not there 10 years ago, or
maybe your skin simply feels thinner and
more fragile. I read every single
comment on this channel, and your
answers shape the videos I create. Stay
with me until the very end, because the
number one item on this list is the one
that transformed the life of Margaret, a
74-year-old retired school teacher from
Savannah, Georgia. She came to my office
looking two decades older than she felt
inside. What happened to her skin in 12
weeks is something every person over 60
deserves to hear. We are counting down
from six to one. Six things you can add
to your water after 60 to activate
collagen, eliminate wrinkles, and
genuinely rejuvenate your skin from the
inside out. Number six is something
already sitting in your kitchen that
almost no one thinks to use this way.
Fresh lemon juice.
What makes lemon juice remarkable for
skin after 60 is not the fruit itself.
It is the vitamin C it delivers. Your
body cannot manufacture vitamin C on its
own. Every milligram must come from what
you consume, and vitamin C is
non-negotiable for collagen production.
Think of it like the foreman on a
construction site. All the raw materials
can arrive, all the workers can show up,
but without the foreman directing the
process, nothing gets built properly.
Vitamin C directly activates two enzymes
called prolyl hydroxylase and lysyl
hydroxylase. And without these enzymes,
your body cannot assemble collagen
fibers correctly. The structure falls
apart before it is even formed. A study
from Tulane University School of
Medicine found that women over 60 with
higher circulating vitamin C levels had
measurably denser, better hydrated skin
with significantly fewer deep wrinkles
than women with deficient levels.
This becomes critical after 60 because
of something called anabolic resistance,
a process where your cells require
stronger nutritional signals to produce
the same output they once achieved
effortlessly. Your fibroblasts, the
cells that manufacture collagen, become
sluggish. Vitamin C is one of the
strongest signals you can send them
every morning. Squeeze half a fresh
lemon into 12 oz of room temperature
water and drink it before eating
anything.
>> [snorts]
>> Room temperature matters because cold
water slows gastric motility, the
movement of your digestive system, which
reduces how much your body actually
absorbs. You are getting roughly 18 to
20 mg of vitamin C, and that consistent
daily dose on an empty stomach builds a
reliable foundation in your blood. Pair
it with a meal containing healthy fats,
avocado, olive oil, or eggs since key
antioxidants in lemon absorb more
efficiently alongside dietary fat.
Moving to number five. This ingredient
has been used in traditional Japanese
and Ayurvedic medicine for over four
centuries, and modern science has now
confirmed precisely why it works so
powerfully for aging skin.
Powdered ginger added to your water.
Ginger contains gingerol, one of the
most potent natural anti-inflammatory
compounds ever studied. Here is why this
matters after 60.
Researchers at Harvard Medical School
documented a phenomenon called
inflammaging, a chronic low-grade
internal inflammation that silently
drives tissue breakdown throughout the
body as we age. Think of it like a slow,
quiet fire smoldering inside your cells.
You do not feel it, it does not hurt,
but it is systematically breaking down
your collagen, damaging your skin
barrier, and accelerating every visible
sign of aging. Research indicates that
after 65, nearly 80% of adults show
measurable markers of chronic systemic
inflammation, including people who feel
completely healthy. A clinical trial at
King's College London found that
participants taking concentrated ginger
extract for 12 weeks experienced a 28%
reduction in inflammatory cytokines, the
chemical messengers that trigger tissue
degradation. For skin specifically, that
reduction allowed fibroblasts to work up
to 40% more efficiently, producing more
collagen from the same nutritional
resources available. Add a quarter tsp
of powdered ginger to your warm morning
water alongside your lemon. If the taste
is too sharp, a small amount of raw
honey helps considerably. Ginger's
benefits are cumulative. They build in
your system with consistent daily use.
For a critical synergy tip, ginger and
vitamin C taken together have been shown
in research from the University of
Arizona to create a compounding
anti-inflammatory and
collagen-stimulating effect more
powerful than either produces alone. I
want to tell you about Robert, a
68-year-old retired firefighter from
Phoenix, Arizona. He started this
lemon-ginger water combination after his
wife kept commenting on how dull and
rough his skin had become over the past
few years. Robert was skeptical at
first. He tried things before and seen
no results, but 8 weeks into this
protocol, Robert told me his wife
grabbed his face in their kitchen one
morning and said, "What on earth are you
doing? Your skin is absolutely glowing."
He had not changed a single other thing
in his diet routine. Number four is
something most people over 60 have never
heard of despite being a fundamental
structural component of human connective
tissue. Bioavailable liquid silica drops
added directly to any glass of water.
Silica is a trace mineral. Your body
needs only small quantities, but those
quantities are critical. Think of silica
like the rebar inside reinforced
concrete. Concrete without rebar exists,
but it is brittle and cracks under
pressure. Add rebar and the structure
becomes dramatically more durable and
resilient.
Silica works as internal reinforcement
inside your collagen fibers,
cross-linking collagen strands to create
the dense interlocking matrix that gives
youthful skin its firmness and
elasticity. Research published in the
Archives of Dermatological Research from
the University of Cincinnati found that
women aged 60 to 74 supplementing with
10 mg of bioavailable silica daily for
20 weeks showed a 55% improvement in
skin elasticity scores and a
statistically significant reduction in
wrinkle depth compared to the placebo
group. After 75, research suggests your
body loses approximately 35% of its
capacity to absorb silica from food
sources alone, making supplementation
genuinely essential at this stage of
life. Add 10 drops of liquid silica to a
full glass of water once daily, ideally
in the morning as part of your skin
renewal ritual. Liquid forms absorb far
more efficiently than capsule or tablet
forms because they completely bypass the
digestive barriers that become
progressively less effective with age.
For significantly enhanced results, pair
silica with magnesium. Magnesium opens
specific cellular uptake channels that
allow silica to penetrate skin tissue
more deeply, work more effectively, and
remain metabolically active for a longer
window of time. Before we get to the top
three, and I promise number two and
number one are going to stop you in your
tracks. If this information is helping
you, please take 5 seconds and hit like
button right now. It costs you nothing
and helps reach people who genuinely
need this. And if you have not
subscribed yet, please do that now. I
post a new video every week dedicated to
helping people over 60 live with more
energy, confidence, and vitality. Now,
number three. Number three sounds
deceptively simple, yet the Baylor
College of Medicine has published
compelling research demonstrating its
essential role in collagen production,
specifically for aging skin. Glycine
powder, a single amino acid that
dissolves completely, invisibly, and
tastelessly into any glass of water.
Here is the fact almost nobody knows.
Collagen is a protein, and all proteins
are assembled from amino acids. Collagen
has a very specific amino acid
composition. Approximately 1 full third
of every collagen molecule consists of a
single amino acid called glycine. 1/3.
Without adequate glycine available in
your bloodstream, collagen synthesis is
structurally impossible, regardless of
anything else you are consuming. It
would be like trying to bake bread with
no flour. The other ingredients can be
perfect, and it still will not work.
After 60, this becomes urgent. Research
from the Baylor College of Medicine
demonstrated that older adults
consistently exist in what scientists
call glycine insufficiency. The aging
body requires more than it can produce
internally, and more than a typical diet
provides. A study in the journal
Nutrients found that 3 g of glycine
daily produced significant improvements
in skin hydration, collagen density,
wrinkle depth reduction in women over 65
after 60 weeks of consistent use.
Glycine also dramatically improves sleep
quality through a second pathway, and
this matters enormously for skin. During
deep sleep, your pituitary gland
releases human growth hormone, the
primary driver of overnight cellular
repair and collagen regeneration. A
study in the Journal of Pharmacological
Sciences found that 3 g of glycine
before bed improved deep sleep quality
scores by 27% in adults over 60.
Better sleep equals better nightly
collagen renewal. Glycine works on two
separate levels simultaneously. Dissolve
3 g, roughly half a teaspoon, into a
glass of water to dawn in the morning
and once 30 minutes before bed. Always
pair it with vitamin C because both
compounds are required simultaneously at
the cellular level for collagen
synthesis to proceed at peak efficiency.
When they arrive in the bloodstream
together,
rate of new collagen fibers is
measurably accelerated compared to
either supplement taken isolation at
different times of day. Now, we arrive
at number two. This is what I teased at
the very beginning, the compound that
stopped me cold when I first reviewed
its clinical data. It has been called by
researchers the single most potent
anti-aging ever identified in nature,
and it works inside your skin cells in a
way nothing else can replicate.
Astaxanthin, available in water-soluble
powder that you simply stir into your
morning water. Astaxanthin is a
carotenoid found in marine microalgae
and the sea creatures that consume it,
including wild salmon. It is what gives
salmon its distinctive pink color, but
what it does inside your skin cells is
extraordinary. Astaxanthin integrates
through directly into cell membranes,
including the inner mitochondrial
membrane. Mitochondria are the
energy-generating organelles inside
every cell. Think of them as the power
plants. After 60, mitochondrial function
in skin cells declines by approximately
40 to 50% meaning your skin has
dramatically less cellular energy
available to repair damage and build new
collagen. Astaxanthin enters the power
plant and works to restore its lost
capacity. A double-blind
placebo-controlled clinical trial at
Hokkaido University in Japan, the gold
standard of medical research, found that
4 mg of astaxanthin daily for 12 weeks
produced a 54% reduction in cross feet
depths, a 38% improvement in skin
elasticity, and a 300% increase in
moisture retention compared to placebo.
300% in 12 weeks from a single natural
compound you add to water. Take 4 mg of
water-soluble astaxanthin powder with a
meal containing healthy fat since the
research confirms that the presence of
dietary fat increases astaxanthin
absorption by up to four times compared
to taking it on an empty stomach. Olive
oil, avocado, or even a handful of nuts
all work perfectly. Combine astaxanthin
with your morning glycine and vitamin C
for what I call the triple collagen
activation protocol. Three compounds
working synergistically on different
steps of the same biological pathway
simultaneously with every single dose.
And now, number one, the single most
powerful thing you can add to your water
after 60. This is what changed
Margaret's life. This is what I believe
belongs in every person's daily routine
from the moment they turn 60. Hydrolyzed
marine collagen peptides dissolved each
morning into room temperature water.
Here is what makes marine collagen
superior to every other form. Marine
collagen has the smallest molecular
particle size of any collagen
supplement, approximately 1,500 Daltons
in molecular weight. Standard bovine
collagen is nearly three times larger.
That small size means marine peptides
absorb through your intestinal wall and
enter your bloodstream at a
bioavailability rate approaching 90%.
Think of pushing a golf ball through a
fine window screen versus a grain of
sand. The peptides enter your blood,
travel to the dermis layer of your skin,
and then do something remarkable. They
do not simply supply building blocks for
new collagen. They actively signal your
fibroblast cells to accelerate their own
collagen production. They create a
biological message that causes your
aging skin to begin behaving more like
younger skin. Clinical trial published
in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology
following 114 women between 45 and 65
found that 10 g of hydrolyzed marine
collagen daily for 8 weeks produced a
65% increase in skin hydration, a 76%
reduction in wrinkle depth, and
measurable increases in dermal collagen
density confirmed by ultrasound imaging,
not self-reported, confirmed by medical
equipment measuring actual structural
tissue density beneath the skin surface.
After 70, your body's collagen renewal
cycle slows to roughly half the rate it
operated at in your 40s. This is why the
decline can feel so sudden and
disheartening for many people in their
late 60s and 70s. Research from the
University of Kiel in Germany found that
hydrolyzed marine collagen
supplementation measurably reactivates
dormant fibroblasts, collagen-producing
cells that have gone quiet with age, and
restores a meaningful portion of their
youthful biological activity. Margaret
came to me after years of feeling like
her reflection has stopped representing
who she was inside. She described
looking in the mirror and seeing her
mother's face, not her own. We started
her on the full protocol, fresh lemon,
powdered ginger, liquid silica, glycine,
astaxanthin, and 10 g of marine collagen
peptides in water each morning. At her
12-week follow-up, she cried at my desk
not from sadness, from relief and
disbelief. The texture of her skin had
transformed visibly. The deep lines
around her mouth had softened. Her face
had a luminosity she told me she had not
recognized in 15 years. She held my
hands and said quietly, "Dr. Lee, I
finally feel like myself again." That is
the only reason I do this work. Dissolve
1 tbsp of hydrolyzed marine collagen
peptide powder into 12 oz of room
temperature water every morning on a
completely empty stomach at least 30
minutes before your first meal. The
empty stomach timing is critical. With
no competing proteins present,
absorption rates reach their peak.
Always take it with vitamin C from your
lemon juice because vitamin C directs
what those peptides do once they arrive.
Without it, you lose a substantial
portion of the benefit. For the most
powerful morning ritual possible,
combine marine collagen, lemon juice,
glycine, and water-soluble astaxanthin
into a single morning glass. Four of
these six compounds, 2 minutes of
preparation, and potentially the most
impactful daily habit you build this
decade. I want to speak to you directly
before we close. If you are 60, 65, 70,
75, or beyond, please hear this. It is
not too late. Your skin is a living,
dynamic, responsive organ that reacts to
what you give it every single day. The
lines and changes you see in the mirror
right now are not a permanent verdict.
They reflect what your cells have had
available to work with, and you have the
power to change that starting this
morning. Your skin shapes how you walk
into a room, how you carry yourself, how
you feel when you look in the mirror
each morning, and the energy you bring
to the people who love you. Feeling
vibrant and confident appearance is not
vanity. It is a fundamental component of
quality of life, and you deserve it at
every age. Caring for your skin from the
inside out is one of the most powerful
acts of self-respect available to you
right now. And none of what we discussed
today requires a prescription, an
expensive procedure, or a specialist
appointment. It requires only
consistency, a glass of water, and the
belief that your body, even now, even
today, is ready and willing to respond
powerfully to the right signals.

SENIORS! Forget Bone Broth! Eat THIS to Build Muscle & Kill Sarcopenia | Dr. Jason Fung


As we age, maintaining muscle strength becomes one of the most important keys to independence, mobility, and a healthier life. After 60, gradual muscle loss—known as **sarcopenia**—can make everyday activities like climbing stairs, carrying groceries, and getting out of a chair increasingly difficult. But aging does not automatically mean losing your strength! 💪 While bone broth is often praised for its collagen content, building and maintaining muscle requires adequate protein, essential amino acids, regular resistance exercise, and overall balanced nutrition. In this educational video, discover which protein-rich foods may help older adults preserve muscle, support recovery, and maintain a more active lifestyle.
